lines.trans: Max, look at the guests in the dining room.
They are ordering our specialty dishes.
People come here every evening.
Everyone chooses their favorite dish.
They do not think about the food's journey.
Which dish travels a long way?
Every dish begins its journey at the market.
Then the cooks prepare the order in the kitchen.
The whole kitchen works for one plate.
The cooks rush very much and get nervous.
And guests only see the delicious result.
For them this is a real celebration of taste.
Soon our usual working evening will begin.

meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
E.g. a school evening. Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Good evening!
I'll call in the evening.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: See?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Не в моём вкусе = not my type. Common masculine noun meaning 'taste; style' in everyday Russian.
Не в моём вкусе = not my type. Common masculine noun meaning 'taste; style' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You are not my type.
She has good taste.

examples.text: Я бы рад вам помочь. Но вы, к сожалению, не в моём вкусе.
examples.trans: I would be glad to help you. But unfortunately you are not my type.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.
What delicious tea!

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: выбирать слова = to choose one's words

examples.trans: He takes a long time choosing a new dish.
Always choose the right words.

examples.text: Выбирай слова, когда говоришь с ней!
examples.trans: Choose your words when talking with her!

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You have visitors!
We're going visiting.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.trans: I'm cooking lunch.
Mum cooks well.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('long').

examples.trans: The pants are too long.
Are the pants too long for Slavik?
Which dish travels a long way?

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I'm thinking about work.
I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Singular only. Common feminine noun meaning 'food, meal' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Oh, bad food?

examples.text: В этом ресторане всегда свежая еда.
examples.trans: There is always fresh food in this restaurant.
Oh no, bad food? Does your stomach hurt?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'order', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('booking') (commission or reservation) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я делаю всё точно по вашему заказу.
examples.trans: I do everything exactly according to your order.
In the kitchen they are preparing this order.
The waiter took the order.

meanings.note: Food, goods, or services. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказать'.

examples.trans: Call and order pizza!
What will you order?

examples.text: Ладно, звони в свою пиццу. Заказывай!
examples.trans: All right, call your pizza place. Go ahead and order!

meanings.note: Зал суда = courtroom. Common masculine noun meaning 'hall, large room; courtroom' in everyday Russian.
Regional/colloquial. Common masculine noun meaning 'hall, large room; courtroom' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Please enter the courtroom.
A big hall.
Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Каждый день = every day. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('every, each').

examples.trans: Every day.
Every person.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: What is your town like?
What a beautiful house!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!
This is my favourite book.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.trans: This is real success!
He is a true friend.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

начаться.gloss: to begin, to start, to break out

meanings.en: to begin, to start, to break out (intransitive)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start, to break out', paired with 'начинаться'.

examples.trans: A fire started there!
The film started at seven sharp.

examples.text: Там начался пожар! Везде пожарные машины и полиция!
examples.trans: A fire started there! Fire engines and police are everywhere!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.trans: When do I start?
The lesson starts at nine.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

нервничать.gloss: to be nervous, get worked up

meanings.en: to be nervous, worry, get worked up
meanings.note: Intransitive. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'рвничать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be nervous, get worked up'.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, вам нельзя нервничать сейчас.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, you mustn't get worked up right now.
I am not getting worked up!

examples.text: Я не нервничаю! Рейтинг Самсонова сравнялся с нашим?
examples.trans: I'm not getting worked up! Has Samsonov's rating drawn level with ours?

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.trans: I'm thinking about it.
We're talking about the town.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ordinary, usual').

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата. Обычный мужик.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.
It was an ordinary day.

examples.text: Я просто пошла на обычный концерт.
examples.trans: I simply went to an ordinary concert.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: They are building a centre.
History will punish them.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Irregular plural повара. Common masculine noun meaning 'cook, chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There is this English chef.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: One completed look. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.trans: May I have a look?
I only had a look.
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: First coffee, then work.
I'll call later.
And then waste will flow.

meanings.note: Новый год — мой любимый праздник = New Year is my favourite holiday
Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'holiday, celebration' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: New Year is a family holiday.
Happy holiday!

examples.text: Это семейный праздник. Как в детстве, с подарками!
examples.trans: It's a family holiday. Like when we were kids, with presents!

meanings.note: regularly, or as a general invitation: приходи!

examples.trans: Come tomorrow.
He comes every day.
If you change your mind, come back. The job is waiting.

проходить.gloss: to go through; to come in

meanings.note: 'Проходите!' = Come in! (inviting a guest)

Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go through; to come in', paired with 'пройти'.

examples.trans: Come in, please.
Come through to the kitchen.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

meanings.note: Arduous path. Common masculine noun meaning 'path, way, journey' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here is a movie: A Thorny Path.

examples.text: Давай, счастливого пути и хорошей дороги!
examples.trans: Go ahead, safe travels and have a good road!

examples.text: Ты сам выбрал этот страшный путь.
examples.trans: You chose this terrible path yourself.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.trans: I work as mayor.
Where do you work?

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Рабочее место = job, workplace. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('working; work').
As a noun. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('working; work').

examples.trans: That means thousands of jobs.
A working day.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for the sake of' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: It's all for us.
I'll do anything for you.
Work, work. It's all for us.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'result' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас.
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you.
This is an excellent result of the work.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас. Работайте!
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you. Get to work!

meanings.note: Fleeting vowel о: рынка, на рынке. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'market' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I always buy it at the market.

examples.text: Мы пошли на рынок за мясом.
examples.trans: We went to the market for meat.

examples.text: Я всегда на рынке беру. Они сами маринуют.
examples.trans: I always get it at the market. They marinate it themselves.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.trans: He keeps his word.
They are building their houses.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'll be back soon.
Summer is coming soon.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

спешить.gloss: to hurry, be in a rush

meanings.en: to hurry, rush, be in a hurry
meanings.note: куда ты спешишь? = where are you rushing to?

examples.trans: What happened? Where are you rushing to?
We are in a big hurry for the train.
Wait a bit, Sokolov. Do not hurry.

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Give me the keys.
Come here!
The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Tableware. Common feminine noun meaning 'plate, platter, dish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.
Put clean plates on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.trans: I was only looking.
Just one.
I was only looking!

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'signature' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: This is signature, specialty.

examples.text: Я могу приготовить своё фирменное блюдо.
examples.trans: I can prepare my signature dish.
The chef prepared his signature dish.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!
